label: PF Backlog 674
title: Review material-change decision API and correct delta-review base
body: Review budget blocks legitimate fix deltas because HIL MATERIAL_CHANGE decisions cannot be recorded through the backlog API, and re-review base selection rejects a valid earlier reviewed head. Add an operator-only decisions endpoint and make delta-budget exemption require a reviewed ancestor base plus a reason citing the latest review SHA.

brief.problem: HIL MATERIAL_CHANGE cannot be recorded via API; review budget blocks valid fix deltas.
brief.what_adds: Operator-only decisions endpoint plus reviewed-ancestor delta base.
brief.why: Keeps review enforcement compliant while allowing evidence-based re-reviews.

objective: Unblock legitimate fix deltas without weakening review-budget enforcement or requiring direct backlog mutation.
acceptance_criteria: The backlog API exposes an operator-only endpoint to append a MATERIAL_CHANGE decision with mode, reason, HIL confirmation and revision guard, and the item stores it for review_budget.
Delta re-review budget exemption accepts any reviewed ancestor as --since, requires the reason to cite the latest review SHA, and rejects arbitrary caller-supplied SHAs.
Tests cover API auth/validation, decision persistence, accepted reviewed-ancestor delta, and rejection of arbitrary or non-reviewed bases.
approach: Add an operator-only decisions endpoint that appends validated MATERIAL_CHANGE decisions through core.backlog.update, and fix architect_review delta budget to accept any reviewed ancestor base with a reason citing the latest review SHA.
risks: A permissive decisions endpoint could bypass review; restrict to MATERIAL_CHANGE, require hil_confirmed and hil:<actor>, keep revision guard.
Arbitrary --since could bypass budget; require the SHA to be a reviewed head and an ancestor of HEAD.
rollback: Remove the decisions route and restore strict latest-SHA delta exemption; no data migration.
evidence: pending

Two independent review-evidence readers now exist (`core.backlog.latest_review_sha` with a `-prev-` filter vs `architect_review._reviewed_heads`); divergence can make "reason cites latest sha" reference a SHA that is not a reviewed head, breaking AC-2's citation/ancestry pairing.
`latest_review_sha` tie-breaks equal `at` timestamps by unsorted glob order → non-deterministic SHA selection.

Tests assert status codes only: the 400 "rejects without HIL" case would also pass on sha-citation/mode failure, and the arbitrary-base test uses `"0"*40` (neither ancestor nor reviewed), so a non-reviewed-but-ancestor `--since` rejection is not covered — weak AC-3 evidence.

Caller-supplied `item_id` is interpolated unescaped into `glob(f"{item_id}-*.json")` in the shipped core validator; metacharacters (`*`, `?`) can widen evidence matching (pattern pre-existed in the router, but is now promoted into core).
NIT: `test_reviewed_ancestor_contract` (`len(h) >= 12`) is subsumed by `test_valid_delta_base_requires_reviewed_head_and_ancestor` — redundant and assertion-trivial.
`from core import backlog` was added above the stdlib imports inside `_start_state_checkpoint`; import ordering is inconsistent with the surrounding function.
SUMMARY: Solid consolidation: router-side duplicate validation was removed, validation now lives in `core.backlog`, and the delta-base predicate was extracted for reuse — reuse/language-rule posture is good.

Top risks: the HIL control is still body-self-asserted while the new error text falsely claims token binding (security contract gap), and the fail-closed config check is mislocated in the checkpoint bootstrap so its availability guarantee is unverifiable.
Tests expand coverage meaningfully but lean on status codes and repo-state fixtures rather than asserting the specific validation path, leaving AC-3 rejection coverage partly nominal.

MAJOR: Startup fail-closed check (`review_material_change_config_errors`) validates `hil_actor` only; the newly required `PF_HIL_TOKEN` is never checked at startup. If unset in a deployment, every decision POST returns 403 with no startup failure, log, or metric — guardrail-2 defence-in-depth (on-startup check) is incomplete for the new secret, so the AC-1 endpoint can be silently dead.

`PF_HIL_TOKEN` bypasses `config/env-flags.json`, which is the declared discoverability registry for PF_* auth flags (e.g. `PF_API_TOKEN`); a required security switch is invisible to operators and has no documented default/purpose/owner.
MINOR: Approved invariant ordering is `authz -> revision -> HIL -> reason/SHA`; the delta inserts the `X-HIL-Token` check before `_guard_revision`, so a stale-revision request without a token returns 403 instead of the contract's 409 CONFLICT (failure-matrix mismatch).
`secrets.compare_digest(provided_hil, expected_hil)` raises `TypeError` for non-ASCII `X-HIL-Token` values, turning an attacker-supplied header into an unhandled 500 instead of a clean FORBIDDEN.

`material_change_errors` reports unreadable `review-material-change.json` as `VALIDATION_FAILED` (400), while the approved failure matrix specifies `CONFIG_INVALID` fail-closed 500 for missing/malformed HIL config.
New `review_material_change_config_errors()` and the `app.py` startup guard have no test, so the guardrail-2 fail-closed behaviour added in this delta is not fail-able/regressable.

Delta-base check extraction to `valid_delta_base()` keeps the reason-cites-latest-SHA requirement outside this helper; no assertion in the delta couples accepted `--since` with the citation check (AC-2 pairing relies on an untested seam).
NIT: `import os, secrets` executed inside the handler on every request; hoist to module scope for consistency with surrounding router imports.
`test_decisions_endpoint_rejects_without_hil` supplies a valid `X-HIL-Token` and only flips `hil_confirmed`, so the test name does not match the behaviour it asserts.
SUMMARY: Delta correctly moves validation into `core.backlog` (reuse) and adds a constant-time HIL token gate plus a reviewed-ancestor helper with tests, but the new shared secret is neither startup-validated nor registered in the env-flag registry, leaving a silent-failure risk for AC-1.
Validation ordering deviates from the approved invariant/failure matrix (HIL before revision; config errors as 400 not 500), and the new startup guard is untested.
Prior MAJOR (self-asserted `by` not bound to `ctx`) and prior MINOR/NIT findings remain PENDING and unchanged; no blocker introduced.

MINOR: Only the negative path is asserted (`PF_HIL_TOKEN` absent -> error present); there is no test that a set token yields no error, so a regression that always reports the missing-token error would pass this test.

The new check uses `os.environ.get("PF_HIL_TOKEN", "")` with no `.strip()`, unlike the adjacent `hil_actor` check that strips, so a whitespace-only token passes startup yet will fail request-time auth (inconsistent fail-closed boundary).

The startup check hard-requires an endpoint-specific env var from a shared `*_config_errors()` helper; any non-API consumer invoking it now fails closed for a token it may not need — confirm caller set is startup-only.
NIT: `import os` executed inline inside `review_material_change_config_errors()` on every call rather than at module scope.
Error text `PF_HIL_TOKEN missing (HIL decision auth unavailable)` states the symptom but gives no operator remediation (where/how to set the token).
SUMMARY: Delta is small, additive, and correctly addresses the prior startup fail-closed gap by checking `PF_HIL_TOKEN` plus a negative test; no AC is broken and no security/data regression introduced.
Residual risk is test seam and consistency: no positive-path assertion, env check not stripped, and no verification that `app.py` actually invokes this helper at startup.
Prior `config/env-flags.json` registration finding for `PF_HIL_TOKEN` remains unresolved but is unchanged and not re-reported here.

MINOR: The `.strip()` hardening for whitespace-only `PF_HIL_TOKEN` has no test: only unset and a well-formed token are covered, so a regression that drops the strip would pass the suite.

`test_startup_accepts_configured_hil_token` asserts `errors == []`, coupling this token test to unrelated config state (e.g. `hil_actor` in `config/review-material-change.json`); a change there would fail an unrelated test with a misleading message.
SUMMARY: Delta is small and on-target: it resolves two prior MINORs (positive-path token test, `.strip()` fail-closed boundary, actionable error text) without regressing AC-1/AC-2/AC-3 evidence.
Residual risk is test-coverage depth on the new blank-token path and assertion coupling in the new positive test; no blockers or contract deviations found.

NIT: The updated assertions match on the substring "PF_HIL_TOKEN" inside error text, coupling tests to message wording; a reworded error string would silently pass `not any(...)` while still catching unset-token cases only via the separate required-token test.

`test_startup_accepts_configured_hil_token` now proves only the absence of a token error; it no longer verifies the overall config is clean, so it cannot detect unrelated startup-config regressions by design (intentional decoupling, but the test name overstates its coverage).
SUMMARY: Delta resolves both prior MINOR findings: whitespace-token test added and the configured-token assertion decoupled from unrelated config state.
No blockers or AC regressions in this delta; remaining risk is substring-based, message-coupled assertions (nit-level).

MINOR: Module-level `os.environ.setdefault("PF_HIL_TOKEN", ...)` mutates process-global state at import time, coupling this wrapper to import order within a shared pytest session (any test asserting token-absent startup behavior in the same process becomes order-dependent).

`setdefault` never overrides a `PF_HIL_TOKEN` already present in the ambient environment (dev shell/CI), so tests may exercise real token material instead of the deterministic fixture value, breaking test determinism.
Import-time side effect is undocumented (no comment on why the wrapper must inject the token); a fixture/`monkeypatch`-scoped setup would keep the mutation bounded and self-describing.
NIT: Hardcoded `"hil-tok"` literal inline; a named constant would make intent and any future rotation obvious.
SUMMARY: Delta is test-only env bootstrap for the wrapper; no shipped-code change, contract change, or language-rule violation, so nothing rises to BLOCKER/MAJOR.
Top risks are test isolation (global env mutation, import-order coupling) and silent absorption of a real ambient token; both are hardening-level for this delta.

fix_impact.finding: hil:<actor> validation method is unspecified: design requires the field but does not say it is verified against an authenticated identity/allowlist, so any operator could self-assert HIL confirmation and satisfy the guard at the new endpoint.

AC-2 requires the delta reason to cite the latest review SHA, but FR-2/design_pack contracts only list "refuse unreviewed/non-ancestor" and omit the reason-citation rule, leaving the AC-2 half of validation unimplemented/tested by design.

New network endpoint contract (guardrail 8/9) states no tenant/subject scoping for /items/{id}/decisions; with only "operator role" authz, item-ID enumeration could cross scope — design must declare scoping or explicitly assert single-tenant.
Design pack does not answer the design-guardrail checklist (CL-008): availability/defence-in-depth, observability depth, and invariant ordering are absent; only rollback and tests are addressed.

Delta adds a new control contract `config/review-material-change.json` in design_pack.contracts.config, yet the same delta leaves functional_spec.config_contract as "review-budget.json: existing policy used unchanged" and the file is absent from declared affected_files — matching design rows were not updated in this delta as required.

Prior MAJOR (hil:<actor> validation) disposition is only half-correct: the delta now specifies an allowlist check, but `by` remains a caller-supplied payload field with no statement that it is bound to the authenticated principal, so an operator can still self-assert `hil:<actor>` and pass the guard — remains PENDING.

Diff contains only `api/openapi.json`; no changes to `scripts/dev/architect_review.py` or `tests/test_review_material_change.py` are visible, so AC-2 (reviewed-ancestor `--since` + reason-cites-latest-SHA + reject arbitrary SHA) and AC-3 (auth/validation, persistence, ancestor-accept, arbitrary-SHA-reject tests) are not demonstrable from this diff.

New decisions route documents only 200/422, but the approved failure matrix requires 404 NOT_FOUND, 409 CONFLICT (revision guard), 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE, 500 CONFIG_INVALID — API contract (spec_pack `api_contract` = APPLICABLE, evidence `api/openapi.json`) is out of sync with the approved design.

Request body for `/api/v1/backlog/items/{item_id}/decisions` is an untyped `additionalProperties: true` object; no OpenAPI schema for `mode`/`reason`/`hil_confirmed`/`expected_revision`, so the contract does not express the HIL/revision-guard validation the AC requires.

Delta replaces `design_pack.affected_files` with only `config/review-material-change.json`, dropping `api/routers/backlog.py`, `api/openapi.json`, `scripts/dev/architect_review.py` and `tests/test_review_material_change.py`; this contradicts `design_pack.contracts.files.route`, `runtime_contract.entrypoint`, AC evidence and FR traceability — contracts are no longer in sync (checklist 8).

`rollback` ("remove decisions route and reviewed-ancestor exemption") does not cover removal of the newly declared `config/review-material-change.json`, so rollback leaves an orphaned control file (checklist 1/6).
